text.t: Glycine is one of the 20 common amino acids that make up proteins.
Its formula is C2H5NO2, just ten atoms in all.
Every amino acid is built around a central carbon, called the alpha carbon.
On one side is the amino group, a nitrogen with hydrogens, which gives amino acids the first half of their name.
On the other side is the carboxyl group, COOH, the acid part of the name.

tour.title: A side chain of one atom

text.t: Each amino acid has its own side chain, the R group, and glycine's R group is just a single hydrogen atom.
That is why the central carbon here carries two hydrogens.

does.t: Amino acids like glycine are the building blocks of proteins.
Cells link them together with peptide bonds, releasing a water molecule each time.

shape.t: With only a hydrogen for a side chain, glycine is small, which lets it fit inside the tight collagen helix.
In collagen, glycine fills every third position, tucked into the crowded centre of the triple helix.

text.t: Glycine is one of the 20 amino acids that make up all proteins, and collagen uses it at every third position.

wrong.t: In collagen, a glycine swapped for another amino acid can untwist the triple helix, a change linked to diseases such as osteogenesis imperfecta.

compare.t: From its farthest atom to its farthest atom, glycine measures about 0.5 nm.
Glucose, also in this gallery, measures about 0.8 nm.

highlights.label: The R group is a hydrogen

text.t: Glycine's whole side chain is one hydrogen atom.
The central carbon every amino acid is built around.
